analysis.title: SpaceX: Got compute?
key_insights: Elon Musk said another 220k NVIDIA GB300s will be fully operational this week and another 220k in November, with potentially another 220k by late December 'if we get lucky'.
SpaceX exited 2Q26 with 1.4 GW of compute and guided for >2 GW exiting 2026.
DB estimates each 220k GB300 cluster equals 440 MW of compute, implying about 2.3 GW exiting November and about 2.7 GW in early 2027.
DB expects the added capacity to be ample for cloud hosting deals, growing inference needs (Cursor, Grok Bot) and training (Grok 5).
SpaceX is building the largest grid-connected battery pack bank in the US, worth 3.3 GWh, to support the expansion.
DB estimates the five signed neocloud customers are worth $54.5bn on an annualized revenue run-rate basis.
Management has not disclosed compute allocation to the neocloud contracts. DB estimates 1.2-1.4 GW, implying $40-45bn per GW, toward the higher end of the $30-50bn range.
DB expects at least a few more large neocloud deals as capacity comes online, given industry constraints, and thinks agentic AI offerings will further increase compute demand.
DB rates SpaceX Buy with a $235 price target. The stock closed at $148.68 on 25 Sep 2026.

market_movers.rationale: Compute buildout is on track to reach about 2.7 GW in early 2027, supporting neocloud hosting contracts, inference demand and Grok 5 training.

risk_factors: Management has not disclosed the compute allocation to the neocloud contracts, so DB's 1.2-1.4 GW and $40-45bn per GW figures are estimates.
The late-December tranche of 220k GB300s depends on 'if we get lucky'.
charts_described: Figure 1 lists compute by site: Colossus I at 230k GPUs and 300 MW, Colossus II phases 1-6 plus Minihard, overall total 1,210k GPUs and 2,410 MW.

Figure 2 lists neocloud deals: Customer #1 at 325k GPUs, $14,973m revenue and 480 MW. Google at 110k GB300, $11,040m, 220 MW. Reflection AI at 18k GB300, $1,800m, 35 MW. Customers #2 and #3 at 110k GB300 each, $13,394m and $13,298m, 220 MW each.
